title.narrative: Emergency Irrigation Rehabilitation Project of the agricultural perimeter of Tchangu, Kinshasa

description.narrative:
Water is the lifeblood for farmer living around Malebo pool which is a very large wetland in Kinshasa, not just for agricultural but also for a large type of livelihoods. Decades of socio political instability have destroyed much of farming irrigation and other water supply systems, which are vital for the substantial agriculture. As the largest area of Malebo pool, Tchangu area is very fertile, were almost 2,500 households practices substantial agriculture in an estimated area of more than 500 ha whose food security and livelihoods are at risk following a sharp fall in crop production due to drought. Since 2014 and thanks to financial support from CAFOD, MAMBELI NGO has intervened through projects DRC 309/2, 403 and 442/1 to defend this site by rehabilitating the dam over a length of 200 m. Unfortunately in front of the extent of the perimeter this intervention did not live up to defend and protect this site which is subject to the calamities of floods happen this season and reducing considerably the production area of the site.
The sharp decline in production will have a negative impact on farmers' income and access to food. Some 10,000 farmers need urgent assistance by restoring the dyke along Tchangu River, were many of the most vulnerable households having lost all or a large part of their cereal crops in that most affected area of Pool Malebo. Furthermore, the present degrading state of the site will not be able to allow the efficient exploitation by the peasant farmers during the great agricultural season which begins in December-January; which justifies the urgent need for an emergency project of agricultural irrigation schemes. These developments will be organized under a framework of a global scheme to restore the agricultural perimeter of Tshangu in line with actions already undertaken by MAMBELI to fight against floods in the area. This is a program to expand the bed of the Tshangu River, by planting protective dike and strengthening existing dikes.
Making agriculture production less dependent on highly variable and unpredictable rainfalls is particularly crucial in an effort to build resilience in Tchangu area. After the construction of the dike the cultivable area will be restored, so this project will help to reach good results for the ongoing projects (DRC309 & 442) funded by CAFOD which aims to increase rice seed production in the Pool Malebo.
